An indexed-color PNG selects the palette-processing path that uses the PLTE chunk contents.
The decoder iterates over every palette entry supplied by the file without bounding the loop to the fixed local array size.
Each palette entry is copied into the fixed local array plte[256]; if the file advertises more than 256 entries, this writes past the end of the stack buffer.
The corrupted stack frame is later used while writing decoded pixels, providing the memory-safety sink that can crash the process.
